whatFailed: update_article accepted a to-many relation object carrying both `set` and `connect`, a combination the docs and the tool's own field description call mutually exclusive, and answered with a normal success result instead of an input validation error, while the `connect` operation was silently discarded before it reached the database.

docClaim.quote: | `set` | Replace all existing relations with the provided array. Pass `null` to clear all relations. Mutually exclusive with `connect`/`disconnect`. |
docClaim.doc: .truecourse/specs/sources/docs.strapi.io/cms/features/strapi-mcp-server.md (line 306; upstream source lives in the separate strapi/documentation repo)
docClaim.section: MCP server > Usage > Content management through prompts > Relations (to-many relation keys table)

observed: Step 21 sent tools/call update_article with data.categories = { set: [cat1], connect: [cat2] }. The server answered HTTP 200 with an SSE tool result, no isError, updatedAt advanced from 2026-08-14T15:19:01.523Z to .573Z, so the write was executed rather than refused. The scenario aborted at this step, so the run has no read-back of the resulting relation set; the code path (see rootCause) discards `connect` whenever `set` is present, so only cat1 is written. Nothing was logged: server.stderr.txt is empty and server.stdout.txt shows only `POST /mcp ... 200`.
impact: An MCP client (in practice an LLM) that emits the forbidden combination gets a success confirmation with one of its two requested relation writes silently dropped: no error, no warning, no trace in the reply. The one place the rule could be enforced cheaply, the strict zod tool schema, states the rule in prose and does not check it.

rootCause.explanation: The to-many relation input schema is `z.object({ connect, disconnect, set }).strict()` with all three keys independently `.optional()`. There is no `.refine()`/`.superRefine()` tying them together, so `{ set, connect }` validates. The `set` key's own `.describe()` string (line 253) literally reads 'Mutually exclusive with connect/disconnect', so the rule is documented inside the schema and never enforced by it. Nothing downstream enforces it either: the document service relation transform keeps all three keys (packages/core/core/src/services/document-service/transform/relations/utils/map-relation.ts:75-98), and the database layer then resolves the conflict by preferring `set`: `toAssocs` in packages/core/database/src/entity-manager/index.ts:149-180 returns `{ set: [...] }` and drops `connect` and `disconnect` entirely as soon as `data.set` is truthy. The generated REST routes never expose these keys at all (packages/core/core/src/core-api/routes/validation/attributes.ts:639-649 maps a relation input to a bare array of uuids), so the MCP tool schema is the only boundary where the rule could bite.

Old engine behavior, new interaction: #26371 is the first surface that lets a caller send `set` and `connect` in one payload and documents them as mutually exclusive.

colleagueFinding.note: Agrees that two mutually exclusive ops in one call are accepted and one is silently dropped, and agrees the schema gap is data-schema.ts from PR #26371. Refinement: which op is dropped is decided in the 2022-era database layer, not in the MCP code. `toAssocs` (entity-manager/index.ts:162) prefers `set` and throws away `connect` and `disconnect`, so `set` always wins. Second refinement: the docs state the constraint but never promise a particular error, so the scenario's exact expected string ('Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool update_article') is the test's own choice; the defect is the silent acceptance plus the dropped write, not the wording.

notes: The rest of the flow passed and confirms the documented relation semantics do work: connect adds (steps 10 to 11), connect accepts both the bare documentId string and the { documentId } object (steps 12 to 13), disconnect removes in both shapes (steps 14 to 17) and set replaces all (steps 18 to 20). Two further distinct defects are visible in the same evidence and are recorded in additionalDefects below: the update reply always reports to-many relations as empty, and `set: null` is a no-op. Only the first failing step is recorded by the runner, so the run aborted at step 21 and never executed this scenario's last two steps (the `set: null` write and its read-back); the sibling run 2026-08-14T15-15-28Z_32215874 of the same scenario did execute them and is cited below.

additionalDefects.observed: Step 14 disconnected cat1 and the reply said "categories":[] , yet the read-back at step 15 showed the surviving cat2. Step 19 set [cat2] and the reply said "categories":[] , yet the read-back at step 20 showed cat2. Same in steps 10, 12, 16, 18 and 21. get_article, by contrast, returns the truthful identity-only array [{documentId, locale}]. The registered output schema types the field as an array of identity objects, so the reply is schema-valid and simply false.
additionalDefects.impact: Wrong confirmation. An agent that trusts the write reply concludes the document has no categories and can 'repair' it by re-connecting, or report to the user that a relation write produced an empty field. This is the reply an LLM sees immediately after its own write, so it is the reply it is most likely to act on.

rootCause.explanation: The MCP collection update handler calls `documentManager.update(...)` without a `populate` option (the populate it builds at lines 280-282 is used only for the pre-read `findOne`). `documentManager.update` then falls back to `buildDeepPopulate(uid)` (services/document-manager.ts:100 and services/utils/populate.ts:441-455), which is `populateDeep(Infinity).countRelations()`, so every to-many relation comes back as `{ count: N }`, the shape the admin panel wants. `reduceToIdentity` (shape-relations.ts:79-85) then maps any non-array value, `{ count: N }` included, to `[]` under a comment calling it 'defensive'. Net effect: 1 related document is rendered as zero. PR #26560 removed `.countRelations()` from the list and get handlers, which build their own populate, but the create, update, publish, unpublish and discard_draft handlers take the document-manager default and were left on the count shape. Single types are unaffected: their write handler passes an explicit populate (mcp/handlers/single-type-handlers.ts:116-118).

Its api tests (tests/api/core/mcp/mcp-content-manager-shaping.test.api.ts) cover only the get and list tools, which is why the write replies were missed.

additionalDefects.impact: Silent no-op on a destructive intent. A caller that clears a relation the documented way gets a 200 and a bumped updatedAt, and the relation survives. The identity-only reply also shows `categories: []` (additional defect 1), so the confirmation actively agrees with the caller's wrong belief that the field is now empty.

rootCause.explanation: `toAssocs` tests `if (data?.set)` by truthiness at line 162. `{ set: null }` fails that test, so it falls through to the partial-update branch and becomes `{ options, connect: [], disconnect: [] }`; the `set` key is gone. In `updateRelations` (line 1195) the clear-everything branch is `if (isNull(cleanRelationData.set)) deleteRelations({ relIdsToDelete: 'all' })`, and line 1198 computes `isPartialUpdate = !has('set', cleanRelationData)`. Because `toAssocs` already deleted the key, the update is treated as a partial one with an empty connect and an empty disconnect: nothing is added, nothing is deleted. The null intent is preserved on the other route through the same function, line 158, where a relation value that is itself null yields `{ set: null }`, so `categories: null` does clear while `categories: { set: null }` does not. The MCP layer passes the payload through untouched: map-relation.ts:75 sends `{set: null}` to the default visitor, which returns it unchanged.

introducedBy.title: use set format (merged 2022-09-30 in 'add first base for reordering')
introducedBy.note: Old engine bug, new promise. Any document-service caller passing `{ set: null }` has hit this since Strapi v4. What makes it a user-visible defect here is PR #26371 (d6f693da85c, 2026-05-27), which added the MCP to-many schema whose `set` key accepts `z.null()` and describes it as 'null clears all', and the published MCP doc that repeats it.
